use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

claims.content: The C2 JU resolves dual designations by initiating track correlation actions, either automatically or manually, upon recognizing that two reported tracks are eligible for correlation, thereby ensuring a single data point representation per object.

goal.raw_text: The C2 JU resolves dual designations by initiating track correlation actions, either automatically or manually, upon recognizing that two reported tracks are eligible for correlation, thereby ensuring a single data point representation per object.

claims.content: C2 JU
All Information Units (IUs) must be capable of periodically comparing remote tracks to local tracks (and optionally common local tracks) to determine if a dual designation has occurred.
The criteria for determining that two tracks represent the same object and the correlation rules must be in accordance with section 4.4.4.3.1, Air and Surface Track Correlation.
The C2 JU must recognize that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation before initiating action to resolve the dual designation.
Correlation involves comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, altitude) with data received on the interface to prevent or eliminate dual designations.

Tracks subject to certain Operational Contingency Constraints (OCC), such as being the subject of a current engagement status message, a pending command message, or being a controlled track, may restrict automatic correlation.
The use case is triggered when a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.

trigger.raw_text: The use case is triggered when a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.

claims.content: The C2 JU periodically compares remote tracks to local tracks to determine if a dual designation has occurred, ensuring criteria align with section 4.4.4.3.1.
Two tracks must pass correlation tests and restrictions twice (tentative correlation followed by a second successful test) before being processed for dual designation resolution, unless restricted.

Upon recognizing eligible tracks, the C2 JU initiates action (automatically or manually) to resolve the dual designation and transmits a J7.2 Correlation message identifying the Track Number (TN) to be retained and the TN to be dropped.
The originating JU indicates any constraints prohibiting reverse correlation in the J7.2 message using the Response Value (RV) field (0 for acceptable, 1 for rejected).

Receiving IUs accept the requested correlation unless prespecified conditions exist (e.g., OCC constraints, conflicting IDs, or simulation/live mismatches) that require rejection or a reverse correlation request.

If a correlation request is rejected, the receiving IU transmits a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2; if manually initiated (RV=3), it is accepted unless specific restrictions like E/C conflicts apply.
If a selection conflict occurs due to Operational Contingency Constraints (OCCs) on both the Retained TN and the Dropped TN, the correlation shall be abandoned until the next correlation check.

Receiving IUs shall not accept the requested correlation if local or remote data indicates a correlation restriction exists (e.g., Identity conflict, different Mode II codes, both tracks are locally derived real-time, or Strength field > 1).
Receiving IUs shall reject the correlation if the Retained TN and Dropped TN would decorrelate when subjected to decorrelation criteria.

If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN and the received RV field is 0, the receiving IU shall transmit a reverse correlation if the new Dropped TN has no correlation constraint; otherwise, the correlation shall be rejected.
If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN and the received RV field is 1, the correlation shall be rejected.
C² JUs receiving a J7.2 message with RV=2 (Correlation Rejection) shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained/Dropped TN pair for a period of 2 minutes.

C² JUs receiving a J7.2 message with RV=3 (manually initiated) shall automatically accept the correlation unless restrictions apply (e.g., different E/C, simulated vs live mismatch, or both tracks are locally derived real-time).
C² JUs rejecting a requested correlation shall transmit a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2.
C² JUs responding with a reverse correlation shall transmit the J7.2 message with the originally received Retained TN and Dropped TN reversed and the RV field set to value 1.

If the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held, and the Dropped TN has an OCC, the receiving JU shall transmit a reverse correlation with RV=1 if the original RV was 0, or transmit a rejection with RV=2 if the original RV was 1.
If a selection conflict occurs due to Operational Contingency Constraints (OCCs) on both the Retained TN and the Dropped TN, the correlation shall be abandoned until the next correlation check.

Receiving IUs shall not accept the requested correlation if local or remote data indicates a correlation restriction exists (e.g., Identity conflict, different Mode II codes, both tracks are locally derived real-time, or Strength field > 1).
Receiving IUs shall reject the correlation if the Retained TN and Dropped TN would decorrelate when subjected to decorrelation criteria.

If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN and the received RV field is 0, the receiving IU shall transmit a reverse correlation if the new Dropped TN has no correlation constraint; otherwise, the correlation shall be rejected.
If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN and the received RV field is 1, the correlation shall be rejected.
C² JUs receiving a J7.2 message with RV=2 (Correlation Rejection) shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained/Dropped TN pair for a period of 2 minutes.

C² JUs receiving a J7.2 message with RV=3 (manually initiated) shall automatically accept the correlation unless restrictions apply (e.g., different E/C, simulated vs live mismatch, or both tracks are locally derived real-time).
C² JUs rejecting a requested correlation shall transmit a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2.
C² JUs responding with a reverse correlation shall transmit the J7.2 message with the originally received Retained TN and Dropped TN reversed and the RV field set to value 1.

If the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held, and the Dropped TN has an OCC, the receiving JU shall transmit a reverse correlation with RV=1 if the original RV was 0, or transmit a rejection with RV=2 if the original RV was 1.
The C² JU transmits a J7.2 Correlation message identifying the Track Number (TN) to be retained and the TN to be dropped to all other C² IUs.
Receiving IUs accept the requested correlation unless prespecified conditions exist which require rejection or a reverse correlation request.
If the own unit holds the Dropped TN as a local or common local track, the Retained TN is designated as a common local track.
If the own unit has R² for the Dropped TN, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is transmitted for the Dropped TN.

The correlation is deemed to have failed if no J7.0 (ACT = 0) is received for the dropped TN after 60 seconds from the transmission of the correlation request, and all associated processing is cancelled.
